In summary, our research is concerned with
the representation theory of the affine Lie superalgebs and the construction of unitary representations.
the representation theory and the Sugawara constructions of the untwised affine basic classical Lie super-algebras, and their unitary representations.
the construction and classification of highest weight representations of affine Lie superalgebas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no unitary representations of the noncompact type I and II affine basic Lie superalgebrs, and only certain spinor gradings yield unitary representations.

the Sugawara construction is possible only for certain type I compact superalgebras and for those type I (and II) superalgebras which yield spinor gradings on rigid two-dimensional conformally-invariant theories.
, in general, there are no unitary highest weight representations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unitarity of the vacuum representation is not enough to guarantee that the Sugawara construction yields a positive definite Virasoro operator.
, for the untwisted basic classical Lie super-algebras, there are no non-trivial unitary representations.
the only consistent unitary highest weight representations are those of compact type I super algebras.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the Sugawara construction is well known for type I and type II affine Lie algebras, the same is not true for their super analogues.
the unitarity of the highest weight representations imposes strong constraints on the structure of affine Lie superalgebs.
the unitarity of highest weight representations imposes severe constraints on the possible values of the central extension and hence on the Sugawara construction.
